findings.message: Ran `npm run check` myself (lint, typecheck, vitest, validate:stories, agents:check, build) and all stages passed: 11 test files / 177 tests passed; validate:stories reports 'the-fog-over-pebble-bay' preview ok and job job-20261020-the-fog-over-pebble-bay-ec899d at in-review, revision 10 (story v10); build succeeded. Also ran `npm run story -- status job-20261020-the-fog-over-pebble-bay-ec899d`: revision 10 validation=ok, gate automated-validation PASS ('schema: ok; graph: ok, 3/3 endings reachable; literacy checks: ok; brief: ok'), gates review:qa and review:literacy both WAIT (no review yet on r10), which matches this being the first QA pass on r10.

New choice `chest-to-bench` (story.r10.json lines 157-161) is a genuine second branch: it leads to `bench` (a full passage with Gran Tull dialogue and its own two outward choices), not an immediate merge back into `gathering`. It differs materially in content from `chest-to-tower` (lines 152-156), which leads to the `gathering` hub. Not trivial filler.

New choice `ask-pip` (lines 181-186) leads to the new passage `bench-shell`, whose content (Pip's shell, lines 191-196) is distinct from what `ask-more` leads to directly (`bench-clue`'s mirror explanation, lines 213-247). `bench-shell` itself offers two further choices (`shell-ask-gran` -> bench-clue, `shell-to-tower` -> gathering) so it is not a single-choice passage and is not purely a pass-through filler: it adds its own paragraph content (Pip's personality beat, Gran Tull's aside about the gull) before reconverging. This matches the revision notes' description and is a genuine branch, not a trivial one.
New choice `clue-to-shed` (lines 242-246) leads to `shed`, a different full passage from `clue-to-tower`'s `gathering` (lines 237-241). Genuine second branch, not trivial.

Checked whether any of the new edges force a reader to re-read an already-read passage to collect an item or reach an ending (the major-finding bar in this review's instructions). They do not: a clean, no-revisit route to the triumph endings now exists that did not exist before this revision: start -> to-shed -> shed -> open-chest -> shed-chest [+soft-cloth] -> chest-to-bench -> bench -> ask-more -> bench-clue [+match-tin, +damp-mirror] -> clue-to-tower -> gathering -> gather-climb -> threshold -> wipe-mirror (soft-cloth, match-tin, damp-mirror all held) -> climax -> turn-mirror -> ending-beam (or call-gran -> ending-help). Every passage in that route is visited exactly once. This revision's new shortcuts (chest-to-bench, clue-to-shed) reduce backtracking versus r9, which required visiting `gathering` twice to collect both the cloth and the clue/matches before climbing the stairs. The pre-existing hub-and-spoke pattern (gathering -> shed / bench, and the symmetric 'go back' options) is unchanged from earlier revisions and was already accepted in prior QA passes (see review-6-qa, review-12-qa on r4/r9); it offers optional revisits, not forced ones, since the no-revisit route above covers every ending.

Traced a route to each ending in story.r10.json. ending-dock (setback, no requirements): start -> to-bench -> bench -> ask-more -> bench-clue -> clue-to-tower -> gathering -> gather-climb -> threshold -> run-to-dock -> ending-dock (5 edges, matches validation.r10.json shortestPathToEnding=5). ending-beam and ending-help: see the no-revisit route quoted above, ending in turn-mirror or call-gran respectively. All three endings in graph.r10.json stats.reachableEndings (ending-beam, ending-dock, ending-help) match story.r10.json's declared endings, and graph.ok is true with no warnings and stateSearchComplete true (32 explored states), consistent with my manual trace.

lockedHint on `wipe-mirror` (story.r10.json line 304) is unchanged from r9: 'You need a cloth from the shed chest, and matches and a clue from Gran Tull.' It still accurately matches the requires block (soft-cloth, match-tin, damp-mirror at lines 295-303) and both items/clue are each obtainable from exactly one source each (shed-chest for soft-cloth; bench-clue for match-tin and damp-mirror, reachable either directly from `bench` or via the new `bench-shell` detour). Hint remains fair.

Checked the engine's effect application (src/engine/story-engine.ts lines 20-21: `uniq([...state.items..., ...effects.addItems])` and similarly for clues) to independently confirm the revision notes' claim that revisiting shed-chest or bench-clue (now reachable by more routes, e.g. clue-to-shed then open-chest again) is harmless: items and clues are deduplicated via `uniq`, so no double-add or state corruption is possible. This is consistent with the prior QA finding on r9 that the narrative-designer's notes point to.

Content integrity: new prose in `bench-shell` is original, age-appropriate, and consistent with established continuity. Pip's shell-tapping habit and the bench setting are established in `start` (lines 94-95) and `bench` (lines 167-171), unchanged elsewhere, so `bench-shell` is not introducing an unexplained object. No sexual content, violence/gore, self-harm, or religious references anywhere in the new or changed passages. Word-set and sentence-length claims in the revision notes match reports/validation.r10.json (sh 25/10, ch 25/8, th 19/8, 0 long sentences, every word-set present on the shortest route to every ending).

Optional observation, not blocking. 'Fen picked up the shell. It was small, dry and empty inside.' has no narrative or mechanical follow-up (no addItems effect, and the shell is not mentioned again in bench-clue, gathering, or any ending). This is a minor loose thread, not a continuity error, and does not need to block this revision; narrative-designer may consider either giving the shell a small payoff or trimming the line in a future pass.

Brief conformance: brief.json sets endingTarget 3 (not the 5 used as a baseline for new stories in general CYOA QA guidance), and this story has exactly 3 reachable endings, so there is no 'fewer endings than brief target' finding here. requiredMechanics (choices, clues, inventory, multiple-endings) are all present and exercised on the traced routes.
